newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's National Front congress opens.
newsitem.headline: France's National Front congress opens.

text.p: France's far-right National Front opened a congress on Saturday to draft strategy for a general election due next year which it hopes will propel the party into mainstream politics.

Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen waved to a standing ovation from the 2,200 delegates as the three-day meeting opened amid heavy security in Strasbourg, on the German border, and thousands of demonstrators prepared to march in protest at the anti-immigrant party.

"Ladies and Gentlemen, I declare the 10th congress of the National Front open," Le Pen, who hopes voters resentment with immigrants and acute unemployment can lead the Front to a breakthrough in the general election in March 1998, said.

Leaders of the Socialist and Communist parties were among thousands protesters who poured into the city on chartered "freedom trains" for a protest march marking a groundswell of oposition to the Front.
Strasbourg's Socialist mayor Catherine Trautmann, who has said she could not legally ban the congress from her city, has appealed for calm and called in 2,000 police to maintain order.
Le Pen has warned of possible violence and the Front urged delegates to remain closeted in the conference centre, cordoned off by police and its own burly security guards.
